input: Audit the subscriptions on my business credit card

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may want to list all subscriptions, or go further to cancel unused ones, renegotiate plans, or reallocate costs — the depth of the audit changes the plan entirely.
This could be a solo review or involve a team/accountant. If others are responsible for certain subscriptions, they need to be looped in for decisions.
Knowing how many months of statements to review determines how far back to look and whether any subscriptions may have been missed or recently added.
There may be a budget cap the user is trying to hit, or a deadline (e.g., end of quarter) that shapes how urgently and thoroughly the audit must be done.
The user may work from raw bank statements, a spreadsheet, an expense tool like Ramp or Brex, or a dedicated subscription tracker — this determines the starting point and workflow.
Done well could mean a clean categorised list, a set of cancellation decisions, a cost reduction target met, or a report handed to someone — clarifying this defines what the finish line looks like.
The user may want to flag subscriptions by category (software, media, services), by cost, by usage, or by owner — the sorting and prioritisation logic shapes how the output is structured.

gold.taskDescription: Review all recurring charges on a business credit card to identify, evaluate, and act on active subscriptions.

questions.title: What is the end goal — list, cut costs, or cancel specific ones?
questions.description: Understand whether the audit ends at documentation or requires action such as cancellations, downgrades, or reallocation.

questions.title: Will you do this alone or involve teammates or an accountant?
questions.description: Determine who else needs to be consulted or informed, especially if different people own different subscriptions.

questions.title: How many months of statements do you want to cover?
questions.description: Establish the time window for the audit to ensure no recurring charges are missed.

questions.title: Is there a monthly spend target you are trying to reach?
questions.description: Identify any hard budget ceiling or cost-reduction goal that sets the bar for what counts as a successful audit.

questions.title: Where will you pull the subscription data from?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has bank statements, an expense management platform, or needs to build a list from scratch.

questions.title: What does a completed audit look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify the deliverable — a spreadsheet, a decision log, a report for stakeholders, or simply a set of actions taken.

questions.title: How do you want subscriptions grouped — by cost, category, or usage?
questions.description: Determine the prioritisation and sorting logic so the most important subscriptions surface first during the review.
